escenes.text: Once upon a time, there were three little pigs who walked through the forest looking for a quiet place to build a house each. The first pig was cheerful but a bit lazy, the second was more hardworking, and the third was the most responsible and patient of all.

When the time came to build their houses, the first little pig decided to make his out of straw because it was quick and easy. The second thought his should be made of wood, a little stronger and nicer. But the third, who wanted to be very safe, worked patiently and built his house with bricks, which was much stronger and sturdier.

The big bad wolf ran straight to the little pig's straw house. He knocked on the door and said, in his hungriest voice: —Little pig, little pig, let me in! But the little pig, safe inside, called back: —Not by the hair of my chinny chin chin! The wolf puffed himself right up: 'Then I'll huff, and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house down!' He blew with all his might, and the straw house flew apart. The little pig ran off to his brother's house.

Without stopping to catch his breath, the wolf ran on to the wood house. He knocked and called out again: —Little pigs, little pigs, let me in! The two brothers, huddled inside, shouted back: —Not by the hair of our chinny chin chins! The wolf, even angrier now, huffed and puffed: 'I'll huff, and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house down!' And the wood house came crashing down too. The two little pigs dashed off to their big brother's house.

Scared, the two little pigs ran to their older brother's brick house. He opened the door and let them in. The wolf arrived and huffed and puffed, but the brick house was so strong that it didn't move at all. The three pigs laughed and hugged each other, knowing they were safe inside the sturdy house.

The wolf, very angry, tried to come down the chimney. But the pigs were very clever and placed a big pot of boiling water over the fire. When the wolf slid down the chimney, he fell into the pot and ran away in pain, promising never to bother the pigs again.
From that day on, the three little pigs lived together in the brick house, happy and safe. And the wolf never bothered them again.
